title: Four requests, zero requirements
seo: BI requirements gathering drill: practise the questions to ask stakeholders before building a Power BI report (definitions, grain, latency, security, reconciliation).
summary: Four stakeholders send one-line requests. Pick the questions you'd ask before building anything, then check them against an experienced BI developer's.
impact: Most BI rework comes from building the right thing to the wrong definition. Ten minutes of questions saves a week of rebuilding, and a dashboard nobody trusts.

body: Four new requests came in this morning. Before anyone builds anything, I'd like to see the questions you'd ask each requester. Don't ask everything: ask what changes the design.

interactive.intro: Tick the questions you would ask, then press Check. Good questions change the design or the numbers; weak ones are answerable by you, too vague, or not the requester's to answer.

options.q: Which costs should profitability include: product cost only, or also shipping, returns, discounts and service costs?
options.why: "Profit" means four different numbers depending on which costs are in. This decides the model.

options.q: At what level: individual customer, customer segment, or account group (for wholesale chains)?
options.why: The grain decides whether cost allocation is even possible.

options.q: Do you want a bar chart or a table?
options.why: A design detail you can propose later; it doesn't change what data you need.

options.q: Which source should the numbers reconcile to: the ledger or the sales system?
options.why: If it must tie to the ledger, posting dates and Finance's definitions apply (see Sprint 02).

options.q: How often do you need it refreshed?
options.why: Monthly after close and daily lead to different designs and sources.

options.q: Should I use Power BI?
options.why: That's your decision, not the CFO's.

prompts.request: Can you just add margin to the existing dashboard?

options.q: Margin before or after returns and discounts, and should it match what Finance reports?
options.why: "Just add margin" hides a definition decision, and margin is sensitive.

options.q: Who should be able to see margin? Everyone who sees the dashboard today, including sales reps?
options.why: Cost and margin are often restricted; adding them to a widely shared report can be a leak.

options.q: Which colour should margin be?
options.why: Not a requirement.

options.q: What decision will you make with it?
options.why: The answer tells you whether you need margin % per product, per customer, or a trend.

options.q: Is product cost available and trusted for all products, including discontinued ones?
options.why: Important, but that's a question for the data owner (Kenji or Finance), not for Jordan.

options.q: What decision will someone take within minutes of seeing the data, and who?
options.why: If nobody acts within minutes, "real time" is a wish, and an expensive one.

options.q: What latency is actually acceptable: 1 minute, 15 minutes, 1 hour?
options.why: Each answer leads to a different architecture (DirectQuery, frequent refresh, streaming, Direct Lake).

options.q: Which metrics need to be fresh, and which can be daily?
options.why: Usually only one or two numbers need freshness; the rest can stay cheap and fast.

options.q: Can the source system handle frequent queries?
options.why: Vital, but ask the data engineer, not Marketing.

options.q: Do you want it in Power BI or Excel?
options.why: Doesn't change the latency question.

prompts.request: Finance needs the numbers to match the board pack.

options.q: Which numbers exactly, and match to what tolerance (to the dollar, to the thousand)?
options.why: "The numbers" is too vague to test. You need a list and a tolerance.

options.q: Which version of the board pack is authoritative, and when is it locked each month?
options.why: Matching a moving target is impossible; you need the close calendar.

options.q: Who signs off that the dashboard matches?
options.why: Acceptance needs an owner, otherwise it never ends.

options.q: Can we change the board pack to match the dashboard instead?
options.why: The board pack is the controlled document; the dashboard follows it.

tasks: For each request, choose the questions you'd ask first, then press Check.
Write the three questions you think matter most across all four requests in your notes.

deliverables.t: A short requirements question list per request

hints: A good requirements question changes the model, the number or who may see it. If the answer wouldn't change what you build, don't ask it yet.

rubric.good: Asked what each key word (profit, margin, real time, match) means in numbers.
Asked what decision each output supports, which drives grain and latency.
Noticed when a request widens who sees sensitive data.
Didn't ask cosmetic or self-answerable questions; directed technical questions to the right person.

retro: Which request would you have built wrong without asking?
Which question will you now ask on every request?
